purpose: Enter the first syndrome rank at which exact UNSAT separation is possible. Classify the simple-graphic rank-three zero-free case when all nonzero projected cycle columns are projectively distinct. A finite PG(2,3) theorem bounds every such abstract zero-free support by seven columns; graphic flow support plus 4-criticality then forces the support graph to be exactly K4. Thus K4 is the unique distinct-projective simple-graphic rank-three obstruction.

setup.graph: G is a simple graph with oriented incidence matrix B over GF(3).
setup.cycle_projection: A is a rank-three matrix whose rows lie in ker(B), equivalently A=H Q for some full cycle matrix Q and rank-three syndrome projection H.
setup.support_graph: F is the spanning subgraph consisting of edges e whose column A_e is nonzero.
setup.distinct_projective_hypothesis: For distinct support edges e,f, the nonzero columns A_e,A_f are not scalar multiples over GF(3). Since GF(3)^*={+/-1}, the support occupies each point of PG(2,3) at most once.
setup.zero_free: 0 is not in {A s : s in {+1,-1}^{E(F)}}.

finite_projective_lemma.name: PG23_DISTINCT_SIGN_ZERO_FREE_SUPPORT_HAS_SIZE_AT_MOST_SEVEN
finite_projective_lemma.statement: Let C be a rank-three set of distinct projective points in PG(2,3). If no signed sum sum_{c in C} eps_c c with every eps_c in {+1,-1} equals zero, then |C|<=7.
finite_projective_lemma.certificate_scope: The finite enumeration is over the constant geometry PG(2,3), not over graph assignments. The checker normalizes all 26 nonzero vectors to 13 projective points and exhausts all 2^13 subsets and their signed sums.

support_has_no_bridges.statement: Every edge of F lies in the support of some GF(3) flow, hence no edge of F is a bridge.
support_has_no_bridges.proof: A_e!=0 means some row w of A has w_e!=0. Every row w lies in ker(B) and is zero outside F, so w restricted to F is a nonzero flow using e. Every flow vanishes on every bridge, contradiction if e were a bridge.

support_is_not_three_colourable.proof: If c:V(F)->GF(3) were a proper 3-colouring, t=B_F^T c would be a nowhere-zero GF(3) tension on F, so t_e belongs to {+1,-1} for every support edge. Cycle-flow orthogonality gives w t=0 for every row flow w of A, hence A t=0, contradicting zero-freeness.

main_theorem.name: DISTINCT_PROJECTIVE_RANK3_ZERO_FREE_SIMPLE_GRAPH_SUPPORT_IS_K4
main_theorem.statement: Under the setup above, F is exactly K4 (up to isolated vertices), and row(A) is the full three-dimensional GF(3) cycle space of that K4.
proof: Because F is not 3-colourable, it contains a 4-critical subgraph J. Every k-critical graph has minimum degree at least k-1, so delta(J)>=3.
If J has n_J vertices and m_J edges, 2m_J>=3n_J. Since m_J<=7, n_J<=4. A 4-chromatic simple graph has at least four vertices, hence n_J=4.
A simple four-vertex graph of minimum degree at least three is K4, so J=K4 and uses six edges.

If F had a seventh support edge, it could not join two vertices already in K4 because K4 already contains all six pairs. Thus the extra edge would involve a vertex outside K4. With only one extra edge beyond K4, that edge is a bridge of F (or a one-edge component), contradicting SUPPORT_HAS_NO_BRIDGES.
Hence F=K4. Its cycle rank is 6-4+1=3. row(A) has rank three and is contained in the K4 cycle space, so the two spaces are equal.

facts: The matrix has rank three and all six columns are nonzero and projectively distinct.
No sign vector s in {+1,-1}^6 satisfies Qs=0, exactly because K4 has no proper 3-colouring.
Thus rank three is the first syndrome dimension where a simple-graphic zero-reflecting certificate genuinely exists.

positive: The entire distinct-projective rank-three zero-free graphic case is a constant-size obstruction: K4.
A candidate rank-three hash with distinct nonzero projective columns is sound for UNSAT only when its support is a K4 cycle space; this can be recognized and verified in polynomial time.
Ranks one and two were universally false-positive, while rank three now has a sharply classified positive graphic certificate in this subcase.
not_killed: Rank-three zero-free projections with repeated projective column directions.

next_target.name: E8_GRAPHIC_RANK3_REPEATED_DIRECTION_CLASSIFICATION_V6_0
next_target.directive: Classify zero-free rank-three graphic syndrome projections with repeated projective columns. Let R be the span of repeated directions. If rank(R)=3 then zero is automatic; if rank(R)=2 the quotient is one-dimensional; if rank(R)=1 the quotient is rank two and must fall into the v5.8 exceptional PG(1,3) patterns. Intersect these finite quotient patterns with graphic flow-support constraints. Seek either polynomially recognizable small obstructions/contractions or a proof that all repeated-direction simple-graphic cases false-positive.
